# Testament of Naphtali — 8
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Greek MS (Codex Cantabrigiensis) | **Section:** Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs

---

Naphtali's testament is about order — the order God built into creation, the order he built into the human body, and the disorder that happens when people rebel against it.

**1** He was 132 years old. On New Year's Day, in good health, he threw a feast for his sons and drank with them. The next morning he told them he was dying. They didn't believe him. He blessed God, and then he told them.

**2** He said:

I was born of Bilhah. Rachel gave Bilhah to Jacob in her place, and I was born on Rachel's knees — that's why she named me Naphtali. Rachel loved me as though I were her own, always kissing me, saying: I wish I had a son just like you from my own womb. That longing became Joseph. Joseph and I were alike in everything, through her prayers.

My mother Bilhah came from a noble Chaldean family — descendants of Abraham — who had been taken captive and sold to Laban.

**3** Now hear this: God made everything with order and purpose. The five senses in the head. The neck, the hair for beauty. The heart for understanding. The belly for digestion. The windpipe for health. The liver for anger. The gall for bitterness. The spleen for laughter. The kidneys for prudence. The loins for power. The spine for fortitude.

**4** He made the body as a mirror of the spirit, and the spirit as a mirror of the body. The senses of the body work together. The faculties of the soul work together. Everything in its place, everything in its order.

**5** So: understand all things in order, sons. Do everything properly, in due season, in the right way. Whatever the LORD commands — do it in order.

**6** You can't tell the sun to hurry up or slow down. It won't obey you. It follows its order. The moon and stars don't change their paths. That's how God made them. So don't you change God's law through your disorder.

**7** I want to tell you about two visions I saw.

**8** First vision: I saw twelve deer grazing. Nine scattered in all directions. Three also separated. This is us — Jacob's sons — scattered among the nations.

**9** Second vision: from Judah was born a virgin in a linen garment, and from her came a Lamb, spotless. On his left stood something like a lion. All the wild animals rushed at the Lamb. The Lamb defeated them all and crushed them underfoot. And at that sight, the angels and all humanity rejoiced. The whole earth rejoiced.

**10** This will happen at the end of days.

**11** So keep the commandments, sons. Walk in simplicity. Love the LORD and love your neighbor. Do not meddle in other people's lives. Because to whatever extent a person walks simply before God — to that exact extent God blesses them.

**12** After saying this, he told them to carry his bones to Hebron and bury them with his fathers. Then while eating and drinking in gladness, he covered his face — and died.

---
*End of Testament of Naphtali*
